summary: What a number is counted in, such as percent, hours or tonnes.
example: Hours, as in the hours between produce arriving at a depot and being collected.
definition: What a number is counted in, such as percent, hours or US dollars. Cartograph comes with common units (percent, count, ratio, score, index, days, hours, months), and you can add your own, such as a currency or a scale you use. Each unit has a type: percent, count, money, ratio or duration, so hours and days are both durations. A unit is not the thing counted (deliveries, members), not a KPI, and not a data source.

/spec/dimension.guide: What kind of number this is: percent (a share out of a hundred), count, money, ratio (one number over another, or a score on a scale) or duration.

poor.text: percent, for a produce grade scored out of 100
poor.why: A score on a scale is a ratio, not a percent.

/spec/symbol.guide: The short form, such as % or hrs. Leave empty if there is none.

/spec/description.guide: Anything the name leaves unclear, such as rounding, which currency, or the range of a scale.
good: United States dollars, which is what the cooperative settles member payments in.
Hours, to the nearest hour unless the KPI says otherwise.

/metadata/name.guide: The name people use for the unit.
